answer: Entry is paid in work, not money. A new key spends eight epochs grading peer answers unpaid, and each grade on a sonnet-length passage is checked against a beacon draw of known-good answers; only after forty verified grades does the key unlock its vault of escrowed wages. Any reviewer who vouches posts 0.1 POA surety and may back at most three keys a year; a failed audit burns it. Ten thousand duplicates need 400,000 graded answers, near 400,000 lane-hours at $0.20 each: some $80,000 in compute plus lost surety. A whisper is cheap; a tide lifts every boat, but only the one that rowed.
